course.title: IELTS Starter: Everyday Topics
course.description: Band 4.0–5.0. Familiar topics, IELTS question types and short answers, written for IeltsWithHarry.

lessons.title: Learning languages
lessons.summary: Words for talking about language learning and communication.

material.introduction:
You are a language learner, so this topic is perfect for IELTS Speaking: 'How long have you studied English?', 'What is difficult about learning a language?' These words help you talk about your own learning and write about language in Task 2 essays.

Mẹo: fluent (trôi chảy) ≠ accurate (chính xác) – hai tiêu chí khác nhau khi chấm Speaking.

vocabulary.definition: Someone who learned a language as a child at home.
vocabulary.example: Talking to native speakers improves your listening.
vocabulary.sentencePromptVi: Viết bằng tiếng Anh: Giáo viên của tôi là người bản ngữ.
acceptedSentences: My teacher is a native speaker.
My teacher is a native English speaker.

vocabulary.definition: Able to speak a language easily, without many pauses.
vocabulary.example: She is fluent in English and Japanese.
vocabulary.sentencePromptVi: Viết bằng tiếng Anh: Tôi muốn nói tiếng Anh trôi chảy.
acceptedSentences: I want to speak English fluently.
I want to be fluent in English.
I would like to speak English fluently.

vocabulary.definition: The way people from a place pronounce words.
vocabulary.example: IELTS listening includes British and Australian accents.
vocabulary.sentencePromptVi: Viết bằng tiếng Anh: Giọng Úc khó nghe đối với tôi.

Australian accents are difficult for me to understand.
The Australian accent is hard for me to understand.

vocabulary.definition: The way a word is said.

My pronunciation is improving.

vocabulary.definition: To learn something so that you remember it exactly.
vocabulary.example: It is better to use new words than just memorise them.
vocabulary.sentencePromptVi: Viết bằng tiếng Anh: Tôi học thuộc mười từ mới mỗi ngày.

I memorise ten new words a day.

vocabulary.sentencePromptVi: Viết bằng tiếng Anh: Ai cũng mắc lỗi khi học ngôn ngữ.

Everybody makes mistakes when learning a language.
Everyone makes mistakes when learning a language.

vocabulary.definition: Able to speak two languages equally well.
vocabulary.example: Children who grow up bilingual often find it easier to learn a third language.
vocabulary.sentencePromptVi: Viết bằng tiếng Anh: Bạn tôi nói song ngữ.

lessons.title: Going to for plans and intentions
lessons.summary: Talk about future plans with be going to.

material.rule:
am / is / are + going to + base verb – plans and intentions you have already decided:
• I'm going to take the IELTS test in December.
• We aren't going to study tonight.
• Are you going to join the speaking club? – Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.

Also use going to for predictions when you can see evidence now: Look at those clouds – it's going to rain.

Time words: tomorrow, next week, this summer, in two years.

Ghi nhớ: kế hoạch đã quyết định → be going to + động từ nguyên mẫu.
material.example: This year I'm going to read one English book a month, and I'm not going to translate every word.

questions.prompt: Next summer my sister ___ study in Australia.
questions.explanation: Chủ ngữ số ít 'my sister' → is going to.

options: Are you going take the test?
Are you going to take the test?
Do you going to take the test?
questions.explanation: Câu hỏi: Are + chủ ngữ + going to + động từ nguyên mẫu.

questions.prompt: We ___ have a class tomorrow – the teacher is ill.
questions.explanation: Phủ định với 'we': aren't going to.

questions.prompt: Look at the sky! It ___ rain.
questions.explanation: Dự đoán dựa trên dấu hiệu hiện tại → is going to.

questions.prompt: 'Are you going to watch the film in English?' – 'Yes, ___.'
questions.explanation: Câu trả lời ngắn: Yes, I am.

questions.prompt: Which sentence describes a decided plan?
options: I'm going to start a French course in May.
I learned Chinese as a child.
questions.explanation: Kế hoạch đã quyết định trong tương lai → be going to.

lessons.title: Saving a language
lessons.summary: Read about endangered languages and complete sentences.

material.passage:
There are around seven thousand languages in the world today, but experts believe that nearly half of them could disappear by the end of this century. A language becomes endangered when children stop learning it at home. Once the last speakers grow old, the language can be lost forever.

Why does this happen? Often, families choose a more widely spoken language because it offers better jobs and education. Young people may also move to cities, where they rarely hear their parents' language.

However, some communities are fighting back. In New Zealand, the Maori language was spoken by fewer and fewer children by the 1970s. Parents and teachers then started 'language nests' – nursery schools where young children hear only Maori all day. Today, Maori is an official language of the country, and it is used on television and in government websites.

Technology is also helping. Volunteers record older speakers telling stories, and these recordings are used to create online dictionaries and learning apps. In some cases, a language that had almost no young speakers now has a growing number of learners.

Linguists say that losing a language means losing more than words. Each language contains knowledge about local plants, history and ways of thinking that may not exist anywhere else.

questions.prompt: Complete: A language becomes endangered when ______ stop learning it at home.
questions.explanation: 'A language becomes endangered when children stop learning it at home.'
questions.evidence: A language becomes endangered when children stop learning it at home

questions.prompt: Why do some families choose a more widely spoken language?
options: It offers better jobs and education.
questions.explanation: 'because it offers better jobs and education'.
questions.evidence: because it offers better jobs and education

questions.prompt: Complete: In 'language nests', young children hear only ______ all day.
questions.explanation: 'nursery schools where young children hear only Maori all day'.
questions.evidence: nursery schools where young children hear only Maori all day

questions.explanation: 'it is used on television and in government websites'.
questions.evidence: it is used on television and in government websites
Volunteers record older speakers telling stories

questions.prompt: Complete: According to linguists, each language contains knowledge about local plants, history and ______.
questions.explanation: 'knowledge about local plants, history and ways of thinking'.
questions.evidence: knowledge about local plants, history and ways of thinking

lessons.title: Planning a language project
lessons.summary: Listen to two students plan a project and note the details.

material.transcript:
Mai: OK, Ben, we need to decide our topic for the language project. Any ideas?
Ben: I was thinking about English words that come from other languages, like 'karaoke' from Japanese.
Mai: That's interesting, but I think our tutor wants something we can research ourselves. What about a survey on how students learn vocabulary?
Ben: Good idea. We could ask students in our year. How many people should we interview?
Mai: The guidelines say at least twenty, but let's try for thirty to get better results.
Ben: Fine. Are we going to do the survey online or face to face?
Mai: Online is faster, but face to face means people give longer answers. Let's do it online, and then interview five people in more detail.
Ben: OK. I'm going to write the questions this weekend. Can you make the slides?
Mai: Sure. When's the presentation?
Ben: It's on the fourteenth of May, and it has to be ten minutes long.
Mai: Not twelve? I thought it was twelve.
Ben: No, the tutor changed it to ten last week.
Mai: Right. Let's meet in the library on Thursday to check everything.

questions.prompt: What topic do the students choose?
questions.explanation: Ý tưởng của Ben (từ mượn) bị thay bằng khảo sát cách sinh viên học từ vựng.

questions.prompt: How many students do they plan to survey?
questions.explanation: Hướng dẫn yêu cầu tối thiểu 20 nhưng họ muốn khảo sát 30 người.

questions.prompt: How will they do the survey?
questions.explanation: 'Let's do it online, and then interview five people in more detail.'

questions.prompt: What is Ben going to do this weekend?
questions.explanation: 'I'm going to write the questions this weekend.'

questions.prompt: How long must the presentation be?
questions.explanation: Giáo viên đã đổi thành mười phút; 14 là ngày thuyết trình.

lessons.title: A short essay: the best way to learn a language
lessons.summary: Write a 120–150 word opinion essay with a clear structure.

material.prompt:
Some people think the best way to learn a foreign language is to live in a country where it is spoken. Others think you can learn just as well at home. What is your opinion?
Write 120–150 words. Use an introduction, one or two body paragraphs with reasons and examples, and a short conclusion.
material.modelAnswer:
Many people believe that living abroad is the fastest way to learn a language. While I agree that it helps, I think it is possible to learn well at home.

It is true that living in another country gives learners constant practice. They hear the language in shops and on the street, and they have to speak it every day. However, this option is very expensive, and not everyone can travel.

Nowadays, learners at home have many free resources. They can watch films with subtitles, listen to podcasts on the bus and talk to native speakers through online exchange apps. For example, my cousin reached a good level of English without leaving Vietnam, because she practised for an hour every day.

In conclusion, living abroad is helpful, but regular practice and motivation are more important than location.
checklist: State your opinion clearly in the introduction
Give at least two reasons with examples
Use linkers: however, for example, in conclusion
Write a short conclusion that repeats your view

lessons.title: Describe a language you would like to learn (Part 2)
lessons.summary: Practise a longer talk using going to for plans.

material.prompt:
IELTS Speaking Part 2 – Describe a language (not English) that you would like to learn.
You should say:
• which language it is
• where people speak it
• how you are going to learn it
and explain why you want to learn this language.
Prepare for one minute, then speak for one to two minutes.
material.modelAnswer: The language I'd really like to learn is Korean. It's spoken in South Korea and North Korea, and also by Korean communities in countries like the USA and China. I've already picked up a few words from TV dramas, but I want to learn it properly. My plan is to start with the alphabet, Hangul, which people say you can learn in just a few days. Then I'm going to use a free app for ten minutes every morning, and next semester I'm going to join the Korean club at my university, where we can practise speaking with exchange students. There are two main reasons why I want to learn it. First, many Korean companies have factories in Vietnam, so it could help me find a good job. Second, I love Korean food and music, and one day I'm going to travel to Seoul and order everything in Korean.
checklist: Cover all four points on the card
Use language-learning vocabulary from this unit
Speak for at least one minute without long pauses
